counterfactual_missing_items: Genetic evidence linking to lamin A/C cardiomyopathy
ECG findings of conduction disease and arrhythmias are secondary, not primary diagnosis
response.rationale: R6 and R4 both rely on the same raw support span identifying the LMNA variant, which is the most specific and causal finding. R6 is chosen as champion due to its more concise and standard label; R4 is a close runner-up with identical raw evidence. Other candidates (R5, R1) describe arrhythmias that are manifestations of the underlying cardiomyopathy, R2 is contradicted by normal left ventricular size and function, and R3 lacks any genetic or structural support.

rejected.why: Atrial fibrillation is a secondary arrhythmia, not the underlying diagnosis; lacks genetic or structural evidence.
Third-degree AV block is a conduction manifestation, not the primary cause; no genetic or structural support.
Dilated cardiomyopathy is contradicted by normal left ventricular size and ejection fraction; also lacks genetic evidence.
Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy is not supported by the LMNA variant and lacks typical RV imaging findings.
